title: Investigate before adding a link.
subtitle: Strategy and challenger contributions came from real Codex work.
takeaway: Discoverability, task timing, report value and permissions remain competing explanations.

proposals.provenance: Real Codex analysis of exported synthetic evidence; not historical reasoning.
observations: Validator corrected a deliberately seeded denominator mismatch: overview 71/155 exposed active admins (45.8%); within-item 49/175 (28.0%).
Matched denominators make the comparison interpretable; they do not make distinct cohorts comparable treatments.
hypotheses: Low discovery may explain lower certification dashboard access.
Lower dashboard value, less frequent reporting needs, or access friction may also explain it; adoption parity does not eliminate these.
alternatives: Test an overview CTA and inspect meaningful dashboard actions, not clicks alone.
If more visits do not translate into useful actions, investigate dashboard relevance and task completion before adding more links.
proposals.recommendation: Treat overview placement as a low-cost hypothesis test, not a causal conclusion. Cross-product association and three fictional feedback notes support exploration, not a proven winner. Keep the within-program option available for focused investigation.

proposals.provenance: Real Codex analysis of exported synthetic evidence; this is not a record of historical Thinkific reasoning.
observations: Within the same 28-day window, certification product adoption is 100/120 (83.3%), compared with courses 102/120 (85.0%) and communities 98/120 (81.7%).

Certification dashboard access is 22/100 active admins (22.0%), versus courses 61/102 (59.8%) and communities 57/98 (58.2%). Dashboard action reach is 14/100 (14.0%), versus 44/102 (43.1%) and 40/98 (40.8%).
Synthetic feedback describes overview-based triage, comparison across programs, and separate focused editing tasks. Three fictional notes cannot establish representativeness.
Distinct product cohorts are not a randomized comparison; comparable adoption does not establish comparable reporting need.
hypotheses: Discoverability: admins may not encounter the reporting entry point during their usual certification workflow.
Workflow timing: an overview supports monitoring and comparison; a program editor may interrupt settings work.

Alternative explanation: certification reporting may provide less useful information, serve a less frequent task, have unfamiliar terminology, or face access or performance friction. The current export cannot distinguish these.
alternatives: Overview-level Analytics CTA: supports cross-program monitoring and comparison; risk is insufficient visibility for admins entering directly into a program.
Program-level Analytics CTA with program filter: supports focused investigation; risk is adding an action during settings work and obscuring cross-program comparison.
Retain placement and improve report value, terminology, or access: appropriate if follow-up evidence identifies those issues; current evidence is insufficient to prioritize it.
proposals.recommendation: Investigate contextual discoverability as a low-effort test, with overview placement as a provisional candidate based on the synthetic feedback. Request comparison of existing dashboard links by placement using consistent exposure denominators before finalizing design. Track CTA exposure, click-through among exposed admins, unique dashboard access and meaningful actions among active certification admins, alongside task completion and accidental navigation. Do not assert causation or measured uplift.

evidence.provenance: Real Codex design recommendation based on validated synthetic evidence; requires human decision.
observations: Synthetic task evidence favors overview-based monitoring and cross-program comparison.
Validated cross-product overview click-through is higher, but selection and workflow differences remain.
alternatives: Overview: show a visible View certification analytics link beside the program-list heading; open all-program analytics. Fits monitoring and comparison.
Within-program: show View analytics for this program; preserve the selected program filter. Fits focused investigation but may distract during editing.
evidence.recommendation: Recommend an overview-level View certification analytics link for this demonstration, pending human approval. Use semantic link navigation, visible keyboard focus, descriptive accessible text, and an Analytics heading with explicit All programs scope. Retain a Back to certifications link. Record CTA exposure and click with placement and scope; measure unique clickers/exposed active admins plus dashboard visitors and meaningful-action admins/active certification admins over the same 28-day window. Check editing-task completion and accidental navigation as guardrails. A click alone does not demonstrate customer value; no uplift is asserted.
hypotheses: A visible entry point at the overview monitoring step may improve discovery without interrupting program editing. Its effect remains unmeasured.
